title: The Ghost of the Free Port Again
premise: Wren Kavanagh, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family aboard Flight 402, has spent seven years buried in the Free Port's gray economy under a polished false identity. When a burner phone he never bought rings with his dead wife's voice on the line, Wren is dragged back into the wreckage: the crash was engineered to protect a smuggling network run by the port's ruling consortium, and someone is using his grief as leverage. To stop a second, larger 'accident' timed to the port's global trade summit, Wren must trade his only leverage—the flight data he stole years ago—to a rival insider he can't trust. In the end, Wren exposes the consortium at the summit at devastating personal cost, learning the voice was his sister-in-law, another survivor who chose complicity to stay alive, and he walks away from the Free Port finally unburdened, if not unbroken.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade auditing the world's free ports and their convenient silences. He writes from a coastal town he refuses to name, drawing on the ledgers, lies, and loose ends of his old trade.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A quiet morning routine reveals his double life: the go-bag under the floorboards, the alias renewed, the ritual visit to the harbor wall where Flight 402 went down. Emotional beat: controlled grief masking constant vigilance.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A burner phone appears in his apartment mailbox, no sender, no history. It rings; the voice on the line is unmistakably his dead wife, Mara. Emotional beat: vertigo—the careful architecture of his hiding begins to crack.

chapters.title: Static and Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He traces the call's signal to a decommissioned customs shed in the Free Port and finds it scrubbed clean—except for a boarding pass from Flight 402, row twelve, seat C. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keeper
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse Brandt, the port's discreet archivist of dirty secrets, notices someone has queried Flight 402's file and flags it to her consortium handler. Emotional beat: cold professional unease; she senses a ghost stirring.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A flashback chapter: the crash, the official report he helped write and secretly falsified, the data card he stole and hid, and why he chose erasure over testimony. Emotional beat: guilt revealed—the lie polished, as promised.

chapters.title: A Familiar Voice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The phone rings again; 'Mara' gives him a deadline and a detail only a survivor would know. Wren realizes the caller is alive and was on the plane. Emotional beat: hope and betrayal tangled together.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Consortium chief Aurel Voss briefs his inner circle on the summit and a 'logistics problem' to be solved before the world arrives. Ilse recognizes the problem's shape: a crash, again. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Old Contacts, New Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He pulls a favor from Tomas, a disgraced air-traffic controller turned drunk, who confirms the original flight's transponder was spoofed. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Wren is no longer invisible.

chapters.title: What the Data Card Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren retrieves the hidden flight data and finds evidence linking Voss's consortium to the crash—and to a scheduled 'maintenance event' at the summit's fuel depot. Emotional beat: purpose rekindled, terror close behind.

chapters.title: The Man in the Gray Coat
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse is ordered to identify the data thief from seven years ago; she matches Wren's alias to the crash investigator. She hesitates before reporting. Emotional beat: the first fracture in her loyalty.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The voice lures Wren to a container yard; it's an ambush by Voss's fixer. Wren escapes with help from an unexpected figure—Ilse, who tips him off anonymously. Emotional beat: survival by inches; trust becomes currency.

chapters.title: Two Survivors
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts the voice's owner: Nadia, Mara's sister, who survived row thirteen, took consortium money, and has been their bait-handler ever since. Emotional beat: rage and recognition—grief's cruelest mirror.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Alive
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia's history: how Voss found her, what he made her do, why she finally turned on him when the summit plan exceeded even her cynicism. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilse's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ordered to deliver Wren's identity to Voss, Ilse instead copies the consortium's full ledger and goes dark. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat's quiet mutiny; belonging redefined.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Nadia proposes the trade: the flight data for the summit bomb's location and Voss's proof-of-orders. Wren must hand his only leverage to the consortium's own courier. Emotional beat: the cost of the secret made literal.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss learns of the betrayal from a mole inside his circle, accelerates the timeline, and orders Wren, Nadia, and Ilse eliminated before the summit convenes. Emotional beat: patient menace turning frantic.

chapters.title: Fuel Depot
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trade goes wrong; Tomas is killed covering their escape, and the data card falls into Voss's hands—but Wren kept a copy and the original orders. Emotional beat: grief layered on grief; no clean exits.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Racing the summit's opening, Ilse and Wren assemble the chain of evidence: spoofed transponder, bought inspectors, the depot 'maintenance' order. Emotional beat: exhausted clarity; the machine of justice assembled by hand.

chapters.title: The Ghost at the Summit
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks into the summit's secure hall under a delegate's badge and triggers the evidence broadcast as Voss's men close in. Emotional beat: the climax—visibility as the ultimate weapon.

chapters.title: What Voss Burned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss, cornered, tries to destroy the depot evidence; Nadia stops him at gunpoint, and Ilse's ledger reaches three governments' investigators at once. Voss is arrested, not martyred. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, delivered inside it.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia faces her own reckoning—testimony, immunity, estrangement—and Wren chooses to stand with her, not against her. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt from shared damage rather than blood.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag, Unpacked
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, Wren unpacks the go-bag for the first time in seven years, visits the harbor wall, and says the names out loud. Emotional beat: resolution—the price paid, the survival finally worth its cost.
